items.reason: zero-kernel implements the Jupyter transport, HMAC, host gate, restart, and limits, but the agent still exposes a native tool catalogue; the one model-facing `ipython` composition is not wired. See docs/kernel.md and docs/tools.md.
No `/refine`, durable supplemental-prompt/memory store, or snapshot rollback for harness updates. zero-agent::self_improve is the narrower evaluate/promote loop, not the Continual Harness.
Roles, policy inheritance, and resume/teleport child records exist, but there is no `rlm()` spawn that returns a handle and no agent_message result delivery.
Teleport snapshots and auto-resume carry child records, but there is no live `list_subagents`/`delete_subagent` API scoped to a parent.
Resident workers and a supervisor exist (T-SES-08), but `zero attach` is not one of the four CLI verbs yet; reattach is covered by resume/line mode.
The supervisor owns routing, health, adoption, restart, and coordinated shutdown; the separate catalog subprocess for saved-session scans is not implemented.
Workers and kernels run as separate child processes with the client's OS permissions; the test-only sandbox is an explicit recovery/spike mechanism, not a security boundary. See docs/trust.md.
The supervisor retries at 250 ms, 1 s, and 5 s, marks a root failed after the retry budget, and adopts live workers. See docs/architecture.md and T-SES-08.
A process-safe lease lives next to the canonical JSONL path, and two concurrent creators converge on one owner (T-SES-06, docs/sessions.md).
The command journal records before dispatch, reports an unfinished begin as uncertain, and replays one effect per key (T-SES-09, T-ACT-06).
Generation/sequence cursors, chunked attach snapshots, and a sidecar offset index exist; there is no file-backed transcript cache above 4 MiB. See docs/sessions.md.
No per-attachment event queue or backpressure: the supervisor has no client event stream yet, so a blocked client cannot be isolated.
No two-phase prepare/validate/commit path for updates across workers; `zero update` swaps files atomically but does not coordinate a live daemon tree.
HeartbeatBook distinguishes user/agent kinds and supports register, pause, resume, and due coalescing; the `/heartbeat` command, clear, and `--follow-up` delivery are not wired to a surface.
The heartbeat book already separates user-owned and agent-created beats, but there is no `rlm_heartbeat.create/list/update` tool.
Cron parsing, claimed ticks, missed-tick coalescing, and per-session persistence are implemented; `zero schedule add` is not a CLI verb and no schedule action is registered.
Goals persist as session state across compaction with token, time, step, and continuation accounting (T-AUT-01, docs/autonomy.md).
Bounded continuations stop on turn/token/time limits and report; configured quality gates and the unchanged-workspace no-rerun rule are not implemented (T-AUT-04 covers limits and cancellation only).
No `agent_message.list_agents/send`, delivery receipts, size/rate limits, or family broadcast. The local MessageQueue covers steer/follow-up for one session only.
Compaction keeps the visible tail, kernel state, and retained status records, and is not treated as completion (T-SES-03, docs/sessions.md).
Named, resumed, forked, and tree-structured sessions are tested; a distinct clone operation is absent.
The branch summary has the six sections and cumulative file tracking, and is used on resume (T-SES-04, T-SES-02).
Cut-point rules, `session_before_compact`/`session_before_tree` hooks, and retained recent state are tested (T-SES-03).

JSONL records and artifacts round-trip with all 13 documented entry kinds, including model/thinking/service-tier, compaction, branch summary, custom, child usage, label, info, state, status, and git state (T-SES-01).
AGENTS.md wins over CLAUDE.md, nearest wins, and the cap is character-safe (T-SES-05, docs/context-files.md).
OAuth device/PKCE flows and an encrypted token store exist for OpenCode Console and ChatGPT; there are no Codex, Claude Pro/Max, or Copilot subscription adapters.
A production OpenAI-compatible adapter plus Ollama covers many endpoints by base URL; the long named-provider list is catalogue data, not tested adapters.
No Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, or Vertex adapters; an OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be configured manually where the vendor exposes one.

The provider trait, base URL/key, streaming thinking deltas, and canonical transcript translation exist; custom headers, per-model override maps, an Anthropic-messages adapter, and full compatibility shims do not.
A seeded model pool with dated source references and a freshness gate exists; there is no models.dev generator or per-provider override pipeline.
Classification, cheapest-above-floor routing, retry/backoff, and the usage ledger are implemented and tested (T-MDL-02, T-MDL-03, T-USG-01).
Fallback and service-tier records exist; model cycling and a `/models` flow do not, and the `zero login` verb is still a typed not-built stub.
No SKILL.md loader or Python-backed skill installation. Monitor definitions can name a skill trigger, but no skill executor exists.
The action registry supports namespaced extension actions only; there is no extension lifecycle, renderer/widget/editor API, or session-navigation extension surface.
The MCP client covers stdio/HTTP, OAuth, tasks, apps, and conformance; shipped skill packages and the documented `McpIntegration` enable-by-login API are absent.
No npm/git/local package installer, convention directories, dependency resolution, filtering, or enable/disable.
The 29-token theme model, 256-color palette, and accessibility checks exist; HTML export and custom-theme loading do not (docs/themes.md).
Every action is rebindable with per-surface defaults and conflict detection; no hardcoded key checks (T-ACT-04, docs/actions.md).
No project/user prompt-template store, argument binding, or loading rules.
The cell grid, streaming Markdown, virtual transcript, input, identity selection, themes, images, host modals, and status bar exist; the subagent tray and a full editor/completion surface do not.
A terminal-free line client drives turns from a JSON script and prints streamed entries; production print, JSON, RPC, and ACP modes are absent.
No JS/TS SDK, `AgentSession`/`ResourceLoader` API, or in-process run mode.

Deliberately replaced by the four product verbs plus machine-level lifecycle (features.md Part 8, CLI surface); the old broad verb list becomes actions, and most replacement actions are not registered yet.
Install docs cover OS prerequisites and WSL notes; there are no shell aliases or terminal-specific setup pages for tmux, Termux, Kitty, iTerm2, Ghostty, WezTerm, VS Code, or Windows Terminal.
Five modes including plan, auto, and manual resolve through one policy matrix (T-POL-01, docs/policy.md).
Overwrite snapshots and undo exist, but there is no git-backed workspace rollback and session checkpoints are not a named operation.
A hash-chained append-only audit log detects edits and deletions; there is no loop auditor watching agent behaviour.
Usage, cost, token budgets, and child/subagent attribution are implemented with roll-up and export (T-USG-01, T-USG-02, docs/usage.md).
docs/trust.md states the kernel is a durable control environment, not a sandbox, and untrusted repositories are inert until trusted; the sandbox spike is recorded in decisions/0001-sandbox.md.
This audit assigns one state and reason per item; the original retain-and-polish/required/capability-gated/not-applicable labels are not preserved as data.
Identity selection and stale-generation rejection are implemented; there is no evidence for cached rows during loading, per-provider failure isolation, or the three distinct empty states.
Selection is identity-based and a stale async refresh is rejected wholesale; preserving typed input across a refresh is not tested.
One central evaluator mints every permit for native tool dispatch and kernel effects; extension, MCP, and subagent dispatch paths are not wired yet.
Keys go through the action registry with per-surface defaults, and render/input loops are tested non-blocking (T-ACT-04, T-TUI-15).

Bounded autonomy, untrusted-content envelopes, and compaction-safe state exist; instruction precedence, evidence-before-completion, and approach-change-after-failure are not encoded as one weaker-model contract.
plan.md M0-M10 and tasks.md carry per-task Done criteria with docs/m*-evidence.md; each milestone is verified independently.

No feature-flag gate: Vim mode, suggestions, voice input, per-shell backgrounding, status scripts, agent teams, worktree orchestration, and computer use are absent; the Android remote control is M9 todo.
No migration-scaffolding lint; zero-review covers security review findings, not this code-review rule.
No lint for options or constants with one legal value at every call site.
No dead-export check for symbols, fields, or methods with zero non-test consumers.
No duplicate-condition or equivalent-predicate lint.
No comment lint; comment style is review-only and not enforced.
Tasks require a regression test for their Done criterion, but no rule rejects incidental, duplicate, or label-restating assertions.
No SECURITY.md or private vulnerability-disclosure policy exists in the rewrite.
No vulnerability-report template or required impact/reproduction fields.
Secret redaction is enforced in logs, doctor artifacts, and telemetry; there is no vulnerability-report template that forbids real keys.
No release support policy stating which branches and versions receive fixes.
Generation/sequence cursors make stale replay explicit and a generation change forces a snapshot (T-SES-07, docs/sessions.md).
The journal records before dispatch and reports an uncertain begin instead of replaying it (T-SES-09).
Leases are keyed by canonical log path and stolen at most once (T-SES-06).
The protocol has event frames, not compact start/delta/end payloads, and there is no worker-to-supervisor delta stream.
Attach snapshot reads and index building are chunked at the store layer; the supervisor does not yet stream opaque snapshot chunks to a client.
No per-attachment backpressure; there is no attachment event stream to bound.
Signed updates verify and swap atomically, but there is no non-destructive prepare/validate aggregate before stopping workers.
The bench gate covers startup, frame, attach (618 MiB), session size, and a heap proxy; fanout, serialization count, throughput, RSS, and a 50-worker stress case are absent.
The agent exposes a deferred native tool catalogue (BM25 search/activation), not one model-facing `ipython` tool.
No subagent admission/spawn API returning a handle.
Authoritative state lives in Rust crates behind the typed host-request gate; the specific TypeScript-host architecture is obsolete in this rewrite.
Teleport and auto-resume carry a child registry, and usage attribution is parent-scoped; there is no live registry that survives a kernel restart.
The trust boundary is explicit: model-generated Python runs with worker permissions and untrusted projects are inert (docs/trust.md, T-TRU-01).
The model pool seeds per-axis grades but does not compute the 50/40/10 coding/reasoning/instruction rubric.
No relative percentile binning over a score distribution; tiers are cost bands.
No coding-exceeds-reasoning demotion rule.
The pool records dated source references, but it does not mark verified third-party harness results separately from provider self-reports.
Dated source URLs live in crates/zero-model/data/models.json; the BenchLM/Terminal-Bench/LMArena/CodingFleet set is not the recorded source set.
Pool entries carry model, provider, parameters, limits, cost, availability, grades, and a derived tier; the SS/Apex five-tier research table is not reproduced.
The router selects the cheapest model above the required capability floor and refuses downgrades for security/destructive work (T-MDL-02, docs/routing.md).
The usage ledger and metrics cover cost, tokens, and context totals; there is no transcript analyser for edit/read tool use or context growth.
The bench gate measures startup, frame, attach, session size, and a heap proxy (T-TST-04); there is no CPU profiler for the coding agent.
No installer render test at multiple terminal sizes; the installer scripts themselves are T-INST-02/03 todo.
No browser-bundle smoke check; the web UI is server-rendered and has no bundled client to smoke-test.
The TUI and the loopback web UI/desktop shell exist; a Docker image is T-INST-02/03 todo.
The loopback web UI uses a one-time token, but there is no `pair`-style link that drives a local session from a browser.
Mesh and teleport crates are implemented and tested; the Android remote-control app is T-AND-01..05 todo.
OAuth/PKCE and device flows plus the encrypted store exist, but adapters are OpenAI-compatible and Ollama only, and `/connect` is not a registered action.
The Ollama adapter detects tool support and runs an offline session; an OpenAI-compatible base URL covers LM Studio (T-PRV-03).
OpenCode Console device authorization and token storage are implemented; the Go provider/plan is not modelled.
Streaming thinking deltas and service-tier records exist; per-model variants and a reasoning-effort setting do not.
`login` and `logout` verbs exist; `auth list` and the auth action group are absent.
The policy has plan/auto/manual modes, but there are no named `build`/`plan` agents and no composer switch.
No general-purpose subagent or mention invocation.
Roles exist for model assignment, but there is no user-defined agent with its own prompt, tools, and permissions.
Policy has actors and a subagent cannot exceed its parent, but there are no per-agent rule sets.
Six-layer precedence with trusted-project gating and env/CLI layers exists; project config is TOML rather than JSON/JSONC and there is no typed file loader.
Themes, keybindings, and status settings exist; terminal title and notifications do not.
Config resolves arbitrary keys; there are no typed model/provider/agent/MCP/plugin/command/permission sections.
The MCP client and namespaced action extensions exist; plugin lifecycle hooks, custom tool/command registration, and a skills loader do not.
No LSP client, formatter integration, or diagnostics collection.
zero-web implements native search/fetch/browser tools, and MCP is a separate client for configured user servers (docs/web.md, docs/mcp.md).
List, resume, fork/tree, export/import, and usage statistics exist; rename, revert, and share do not.
Auto-compaction retains the visible tail and kernel state, and branch summaries have the documented six sections (T-SES-03, T-SES-04).
A durable queue with steer/follow-up exists; multi-session tabs do not.
Managed overwrites take a snapshot and support undo; there is no git-backed rollback.
No share links or local share/pair flow; the loopback web UI is not a share mechanism.
The mode-by-action-class matrix and approvals exist; there are no per-tool allow/ask/deny rules with user/project scopes.
A central policy evaluator mints permits for native tools and kernel effects; extension, MCP, and subagent calls are not wired.
Host-owned approval modals bind the exact action hash, expire, and keep a durable decision record (T-POL-05, T-TUI-13).
No `serve` HTTP API or OpenAPI description; the web UI is loopback-only.
No JS/TS or Python SDK and no ACP stdio server.
`doctor --json` and the line-mode client exist; there is no one-shot headless run mode.
No VS Code, JetBrains, or Zed/ACP integration.
The CLI is exactly `resume`, `login`, `logout`, and `doctor`; an unknown verb prints the closest action name and exits non-zero (T-FND-11).
All machine-level verbs exist and service/update/uninstall are tested; platform installers are T-INST-02/03 todo.
The action registry, policy, and idempotency exist, but most listed verbs are not registered actions reachable from every surface, SDK, ACP, or MCP server mode.
The CI matrix builds Windows (x64/ARM64), macOS (x64/ARM64), and Linux (x64/ARM64), and WSL is covered by the Linux tests (T-TST-01).
Image/file attachments, typed blocks, and `@` references exist; path autocomplete does not.
Provider streaming honours cancellation and queue steering defers to a tool boundary, but no interrupt/cancel action is registered on a surface.
Signed/hash-verified updates and `update --check` are implemented (T-INST-04).
Every theme token is overridable and every action is rebindable (T-TUI-09, T-ACT-04).
No localisation layer or message catalogue; user-facing strings are English literals.
Usage, cost, and token statistics with attribution and export are implemented (T-USG-01, T-USG-02).
No GitHub issue or pull-request integration.
No Dockerfile or container deployment; packaging is T-INST-02/03 todo.
